title: First Thing: Trump, Xi and Putin hold historic trilateral meeting in China
summary: The three leaders spoke about international peace and nuclear weapons as Trump called Putin a ‘friend’. Plus, yes, GTA VI is really finally here, and the critics have their verdict:…

blocks.text: Good morning. Donald Trump has met Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, and said the three leaders were “really making history”. The trilateral meeting lasted roughly an hour and a half, according to Chinese state media. On arrival the US president described his Russian counterpart as “my friend”.

Putin told Xi and Trump that their countries shared “many converging interests” when it came to resolving conflicts, including the full-scale war in Ukraine, which the Russian president started in 2022.

Trump said the three countries were “uniquely positioned” to discuss nuclear weapons, while Xi said “every effort must be made to prevent nuclear war” and that nuclear weapons ⁠should be comprehensively prohibited and completely ⁠destroyed.

China released a readout of an earlier Trump-Xi meeting, with the tone being largely positive, but containing a warning on Taiwan and a call to strengthen communication on trade and AI. Trump has now departed from China.

items: What was unusual about China’s welcome to the Japanese delegation? Apec’s Chinese hosts went out of their way to give world leaders a warm welcome as they arrived in Shenzhen, with one exception. Japan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, had to make do with a modest guard of honour and a welcome from a relatively junior Chinese government official.
The Guardian is live blogging the Apec summit. You can follow it here.

blocks.caption: Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive of Anthropic. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images

blocks.text: Positioned for one of the biggest IPOs in history, Anthropic set the share price for its debut on the US stock market at $83, above its earlier estimates. The firm is slated to begin trading on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT, with its chief executive, Dario Amodei, and other cofounders ringing the bell to open the Nasdaq exchange. Graeme Wearden has the latest on our business live blog.

items: What is the latest warning on the environmental impact of AI? The world’s datacentres will create 70% more carbon emissions within the next four years as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power their AI growth agendas, according to the world’s energy watchdog.

Who has been accused of spying in Silicon Valley? The US Department of Justice has accused a Russian national of spying on employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company in an alleged effort to gather intelligence for Russia. Igor D’iu had been indicted on multiple charges.

Why have four Maryland high school students sued after an AI error? Four current and former students at a Maryland high school have filed a lawsuit a year after armed police detained them, prompted by an AI alert that mistook a bag of Doritos for a gun, in an incident that left them “fearing for their lives”.

blocks.text: Elon Musk claims ‘I’m not Maga’ and says he regrets vast sums to back Republicans

blocks.caption: Elon Musk at CPAC. Photograph: Andrew Harnik/Getty Images

blocks.text: Elon Musk has denied being Maga despite previously aligning himself intensely with Trump. In an interview, Musk admitted that his record midterm spending had “failed”, and that he felt “pretty foolish” for spending such a sum, saying: “If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.”

After Trump took office for the second time in 2025, Musk served for 180 days heading the so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge) within Trump’s administration. Musk famously declared at a 2024 campaign rally in Madison Square Garden: “I’m not just Maga. I’m dark, gothic Maga.”
Myanmar committed acts of genocide against Rohingya minority, world’s top court rules

blocks.caption: A Bangladeshi man helps Rohingya Muslim refugees to disembark from a boat. Photograph: Fred Dufour/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Myanmar committed acts of genocide against its Rohingya minority during “clearance operations” nearly a decade ago, the world’s highest court has ruled.

The judgment from the international court of justice, which has never previously found a state responsible for genocide, ends a seven-year legal battle and is seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes.
In other news …

blocks.caption: Hakeem Jeffries. Photograph: J Scott Applewhite/AP

items: Democrats have resoundingly nominated Hakeem Jeffries to serve as speaker of the House when the new Congress is sworn in next year, teeing him up to become the first Black lawmaker to lead the chamber.

US authorities have admitted altering the translation of an extradition request for James “Fergie” Chambers from English into Spanish. The translated version attributed violent and illegal actions to the wealthy activist and philanthropist that were not in the original.
A Florida pastor has been convicted of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse. Christian Emmanuel Sanon has dual Haitian-American citizenship.
An anti-vaccine group once led by Robert F Kennedy Jr is back on Facebook and Instagram after previously being banned.
One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

Parts of Bangladesh were shut down as protests by supporters of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina sparked clashes, bomb blasts and arson attacks, with the ancestral home ⁠of the former leader Muhammad Yunus set ablaze in the violence.
